newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Standard and Poor's rates NZ Post AA+/A-1+.
newsitem.headline: Standard and Poor's rates NZ Post AA+/A-1+.

text.p: Ratings agency Standard and Poor's on Thursday said it had assigned its AA+/A-1+ ratings to New Zealand Post Ltd, reflecting a solid business base, diversification of revenues, and a reasonably conservative financial profile.
"These ratings are further underpinned by NZ Post being wholly owned by the New Zealand government," S&P said in a statement.

Offsetting these positive factors were a projected increase in gearing, the possible removal of statutory protection, and the potential reduction of the postal market as a result of technological erosion.
S&P said it believed competition for the standard letter would not increase significantly over the next few years even if NZ Post's statutory protection was removed in the near future.
"The rating outlook is stable," S&P said.
"If it proceeds, the final stage of deregulating the New Zealand postal market is unlikely to have any immediate impact on NZ Post's business or financial profile.
"However, technological erosion and competition from niche players requires NZ Post to remain innovative if it is to maintain and grow current revenue streams."
NZ Post said the ratings, which are the same as those assigned to the New Zealand government, were a statement of confidence in its future business prospects.
NZ Post reported a profit for the six months to September 30, 1996, of NZ$22.2 million following a record $75.2 million profit for the 1995/96 year.
As at September 30, the company reported total assets of $402.5 million, equity of $185.6 million and a six monthly turnover of $334.1 million.
